newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom NZ thumbs nose at politics, hits new highs.
newsitem.headline: Telecom NZ thumbs nose at politics, hits new highs.

text.p: Shares in Telecom Corp of New Zealand rose to a domestic all-time high in early Monday trade, seemingly unfazed by the prospect of a left-of-centre government emerging from the October 12 general election.
New Zealand's largest listed company climbed eleven cents to NZ$7.16, easily surpassing its previous all-time high of $7.05 posted at the close last Friday when it jumped 10 cents.
Brokers said the gains were due to the share market's general strength and to a strong bond market.

"It's partly market specific, it's also partly that the bond market has just kept on rallying. I don't know that there's any company specific news that's pushed it along," said Tim Koller at Hendry Hay McIntosh.
The high yielding Telecom stock is seen sensitive to bond market moves.
Wayne Schuler at Cavill White said Telecom was playing catch-up in New Zealand having traded up towards $7.20 in the United States late last Friday as the Dow moved to a new all-time high.
Brokers said it did not appear likely that Telecom would trade domestically as high as it had in the U.S., but it had been hard to anticipate New Zealand market movements of late.

"At the moment it appears that there are enough people willing to lighten their load in the stock to stop it, but the market has been extremely strong, so I wouldn't put my money against it (trading higher)," Koller said.
Brokers said the market had paid little heed to two political opinion polls published over the weekend, and its strength continued to surprise.
The polls showed support growing for the opposition Labour Party at the expense of the governing conservative National Party.
The three main left of centre parties -- Labour, New Zealand First and the Alliance -- collectively hold the majority of the vote. A general election will be held in six days on October 12.
Koller said the market had gone past hoping that National was going to be re-elected as the leader of the next government.
"Now it's like 'if the Left gets in, well at least it's going to be Labour at the helm'," he said.
"It's obviously not ideal, but it certainly hasn't put investors off, that's for sure."
At 12.55 p.m. (2355 GMT), Telecom was at $7.16 on volume of 3.62 million shares.
